Recovering the seat assignments from the loops' logs, so they restart with the same agents.The last run's state is intact: each loop saved its in-flight job, and both are set up to resume from it. Starting both loops with the same seats as before.Both topology loops are running again, with the same agents in the same roles, and each has picked up where it stopped on 29 September.

| Loop | Owner | Author (also repairs) | Reviewer | Probe and strategy | Worklist |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `topo1` | topo-1 | topo-2 | topo-3 | topo-4 | `worklist.edn`: 5 open, 3 blocked, 1 waiting on the owner, 1 awaiting review |
| `topo2` | topo-5 | topo-6 | topo-7 | topo-8 | `worklist2.edn`: 1 open, 4 blocked, 1 awaiting review |

**Where they picked up:** each loop's interrupted job had finished before the stop, and its result was saved. On restart both loops read those results. Both jobs were author attempts that stopped short:
- topo1's was the t98a06 part (a) adapter.
- topo2's was the t94a08 affine-chart homeomorphism.

Each loop then sent its job to its reviewer (topo-3 and topo-7), which is the next step in the normal flow.

**Checked:**
- Every topo seat is on gpt-5.6-sol according to the roster, and the newest Codex session file confirms it.
- Repair jobs go to each loop's author seat. When a loop runs out of repairs, it escalates to me.
- Both loops run in `futon-agents.slice`.

The build loop for the five non-topology problems is still running on the solve seats alongside them.

Inspect with `systemctl --user status topo1 topo2`; the logs are `holes/labs/topology-contract/runs{,2}/build-loop.log`.
